$comment: Why each entry in package.json's `overrides` block exists.
An override is a permanent, silent edit to the dependency graph. Nothing in
`bun audit` or Dependabot ever revisits one, so without this file the reason
for each lives only in a commit message and the answer to 'can this go yet?'
is nobody's. That matters because a STALE override is not inert: it keeps
forcing a version on consumers that have since moved on, which is exactly how
a bare `brace-expansion` key once dragged minimatch@9's `^2.0.2` copies up to
5.x and killed it on a dropped default export.
`src/__tests__/dependency-overrides.test.ts` keeps this file and package.json
in lockstep, so an override added without a reason fails the suite. It also
checks each override is actually IN EFFECT in bun.lock — adding one to
package.json does not move an already-resolved package, so an override can
read as protection in review while installing the vulnerable copy.
Removal is deliberately a human decision, and `dropWhen` below is written for
a human to evaluate. Auto-detecting staleness was tried and does not work: a
fresh resolution always picks the highest version satisfying every consumer's
range, so 'would this still be safe without the override?' answers yes for
every entry, always — including ones that are genuinely load-bearing. The
override is insurance against a future consumer whose range caps the package
below the fix, and insurance does not look used until it pays out.
Keys must be major-scoped (`pkg@N`), never bare — a bare key forces EVERY
copy in the tree to the new version regardless of what each consumer declared.
`overrides` documents the ROOT package.json; `adminUiOverrides` documents
admin-ui/package.json. admin-ui is a separate project with its own lockfile,
and it went ungated for both of the properties above until 2026-08-17: its
block had accumulated an undocumented `postcss` entry with a BARE key — added
in a0219a8, the same commit whose message explains at length why keys must be
major-scoped. Nothing caught it, because the test only ever read the root.

brace-expansion@5.reason: DoS via unbounded expansion in 5.0.7. Reached the tree through minimatch under eslint / typescript-eslint / stryker.
brace-expansion@5.dropWhen: Every consumer of the 5.x line resolves to >= 5.0.8 on its own. Scoped to major 5 deliberately: the 2.x copies under minimatch@9 must NOT be moved.

fast-uri@3.reason: Host confusion via a backslash authority introducer, below 3.1.5. Arrives via ajv, which is exact-pinned at 8.18.0 and cannot simply be bumped.
fast-uri@3.dropWhen: ajv's own dependency range floors fast-uri at >= 3.1.5.

hono@4.reason: ReDoS in the CORS middleware below 4.12.34. Transitive via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk > @hono/node-server; the gateway itself runs Express and never calls hono.
hono@4.dropWhen: @hono/node-server (as pulled by the MCP SDK) floors hono at >= 4.12.34.

ip-address@10.reason: Three parsing flaws at or below 10.3.0 (leading-zero octets read as decimal, CIDR suffix suppressing special-use classification, IPv4-mapped/NAT64 misclassification). All three are worded as SSRF bypasses, which reads alarming here and is worth stating precisely: this gateway's SSRF pinning uses ipaddr.js, a DIFFERENT library. ip-address arrives only via @modelcontextprotocol/sdk > express-rate-limit, so the real exposure was per-IP rate-limit evasion.
ip-address@10.dropWhen: express-rate-limit (as pulled by the MCP SDK) floors ip-address at > 10.3.0.

js-yaml@4.reason: Quadratic CPU consumption resolving `!!omap`, at or below 4.3.0 (the CVE-2026-59870 fix was not backported to the 4.x line until 4.3.1). Reaches the tree only through @commitlint/cli > @commitlint/load > cosmiconfig, i.e. a devDependency that parses this repo's own commitlint config during the commit-msg hook — never attacker-controlled input. Worth stating precisely, because the gateway does parse untrusted YAML (OpenAPI specs at registration, config import): that path uses the `yaml` package, a different library, and nothing under src/ imports js-yaml at all.
js-yaml@4.dropWhen: cosmiconfig (as pulled by @commitlint/load) floors js-yaml at >= 4.3.1; its range is a permissive ^4.1.0, so this lands as soon as a fresh resolve is allowed to pick the patched version.

brace-expansion@5.reason: DoS via unbounded expansion in 5.0.7. Same advisory and same arrival path as the root entry — minimatch under eslint / typescript-eslint — but admin-ui resolves its own tree from its own lockfile, so the root override does not reach it.
brace-expansion@5.dropWhen: Every consumer of the 5.x line resolves to >= 5.0.8 on its own. Scoped to major 5 deliberately: the 2.x copies under minimatch@9 must NOT be moved.

js-yaml@4.reason: Quadratic CPU consumption resolving `!!omap`, at or below 4.3.0. Arrives via openapi-typescript > @redocly/openapi-core, which is build-time only: it regenerates types/openapi.generated.ts during `typecheck`/`build` and no js-yaml reaches the shipped SPA bundle. Worth recording what this case proves, because it is easy to over-generalise: @redocly/openapi-core pins js-yaml at an EXACT "4.3.0" and the override moved it anyway, so an exact pin is NOT by itself beyond an override's reach. What is beyond reach is a NESTED duplicate — measured on the qs/typed-rest-client case in security.yml, where a fresh resolve carrying a `qs@6` override still left `typed-rest-client/qs` on 6.15.1. js-yaml had a single hoisted copy, so there was nothing for the override to fail to collapse.
js-yaml@4.dropWhen: @redocly/openapi-core moves its exact js-yaml pin to >= 4.3.1.

nanoid@3.reason: Custom generators can loop indefinitely when the requested size is zero, below 3.3.18. Reaches the tree only under postcss (via vite, @vue/compiler-sfc and vue-router), i.e. the build-time CSS pipeline, which calls nanoid with postcss's own fixed size and never with attacker input.
nanoid@3.dropWhen: postcss floors nanoid at >= 3.3.18; its range is a permissive ^3.3.16.

postcss@8.reason: Path traversal in previous-source-map auto-loading: an attacker-controlled `sourceMappingURL` reads an arbitrary .map file when `from` is unset. The floor was raised from ^8.5.18 to ^8.5.23 on 2026-08-17 — ^8.5.18 covered only the first advisory, and the follow-up GHSA-fxqj-rqcc-2cmp (incomplete fix, affecting <= 8.5.22) left the declared floor pointing at a version that is still vulnerable. Build-time only; the gateway serves the compiled CSS, not postcss.
postcss@8.dropWhen: vite and @vue/compiler-sfc both floor postcss at >= 8.5.23.
